Cameron Bancroft: Former Australia batter says he feels 'very free' after 'telling the truth' with Sandpapergate claims
Cameron Bancroft says he "never meant to point fingers or implicate others; "I just wanted to, for my own peace, to tell the truth;" in making his statement on the 2018 ball tampering scandal; meanwhile, Pat Cummins' manager says Test captain has been "consistent and adamant from day one"
Thursday 19 November 2026 07:58, UK
Cameron Bancroft says he feels "very free" following his explosive claims about the Sandpapergate scandal.
In a 4,000-word statement in The West Australian newspaper on Wednesday, Bancroft broke his silence on revelations in Usman Khawaja's new book, claiming that Cummins' press conference denying the allegations was the "final straw" for him, revealing that the entire bowling unit maintained full knowledge of the extensive use of sandpaper.
Bancroft saw his career turned upside after being suspended for his part in the 2018 incident alongside then captain Steve Smith and vice-captain David Warner. Those were the only three players to be punished.
Speaking to local media on Thursday, Bancroft said: "I never meant to point fingers or implicate others; I just wanted to, for my own peace, to tell the truth.
"This has been a burden that I've carried with me for such a long period of time but I feel very free and I feel very happy that I've been able to do that."
Footage on social media on Thursday also showed Cummins being approached for comment by local TV reporters when leaving his house for training with New South Wales. The Australian Test captain declined to address Bancroft's remarks.
A statement from his manager, Neil Maxwell, said: "Pat's position hasn't changed in eight years. He's been consistent and adamant from day one.
"Pat feels for Cam [Bancroft] of course. He has been through a lot. We would urge people to again read Pat's interview transcript. There is nothing he hasn't answered. And that includes in response to what Cam has now said."
Bancroft's statement has heaped pressure on Test captain Cummins, with Australia's next red-ball series against New Zealand beginning on December 9.
The claims come in the wake of a furore of discussion around the 2018 scandal, with Khawaja's book first bringing to light claims that the entire team knew about the use of sandpaper.
Khawaja also alleged that discussions about ball-tampering had been held "openly and lightheartedly" across the entire squad, involving not just the batters, bowlers and coaching staff but the wider team.
Cummins dismissed Khawaja's claims as "complete and utter nonsense" during a sensational 68-minute press conference last Friday.
Bancroft's statement came just after Cricket Australia announced an independent forum to explore the scandal, stating that players could share their version of events without fears of reprisals - a decision which Khawaja and David Warner have questioned.
digest_he: שחקן הקריקט לשעבר של נבחרת אוסטרליה, קמרון בנקרופט, הצהיר כי הוא מרגיש הקלה גדולה לאחר שפרסם הצהרה מפורטת בת 4,000 מילים על פרשת שיוף הכדור הידועה משנת 2018. בנקרופט טען כי כל שחקני ההגשה ידעו על השימוש בנייר שיוף, וכי מסיבת העיתונאים שבה הכחיש קפטן נבחרת אוסטרליה הנוכחי, פאט קאמינס, את הדברים היוותה נקודת שבר עבורו. בעוד שמנג'ר של קאמינס דחה את הטענות וציין כי עמדתו של הקפטן נותרה עקבית לאורך השנים, ההצהרה מחדשת את הלחץ על קראקט אוסטרליה ועל הנבחרת לקראת סדרת משחקים הקרובה.
